design.name: 饕餮
design.brief: Taotie (饕餮), one of the Four Fiends of Chinese myth, the insatiable glutton whose face is the taotie mask on Shang dynasty bronzes ('a goat's body with a human-like face, eyes under its armpits, tiger's teeth and human-like claws'). A squat, massive beast about 5 m tall at the shoulder: a heavy ram-like body with two big curling horns, clad in thick verdigris-green bronze plates engraved with squared cloud-and-thunder spirals (雷纹); its HEAD is an enormous bronze ritual-mask face as wide as its chest, with a bulging brow ridge, flaring nostrils, empty dark eye sockets and a gaping mouth full of tiger fangs, sculpted water pouring into it as it swallows a lake. Its real eyes are NOT on the face: two glowing magenta-violet eyes sit under the front legs in the armpits (weak spots), shown in the rearing main pose. Clawed paws, magenta lightning in the plate seams. Gluttonous and terrifying; a stylized bronze-mask monster, not a realistic person.
design.style_note: Stylization: cartoon game proportions in the same family as the earlier rosters (jerboa soldier, fire rat, sancai tomb beast, huodou sighthound): chunky simplified masses, oversized heads and paws, toy-like readable forms with clean bevelled edges. Lightning is painted as OPAQUE glowing magenta-violet zig-zag veins and solid sculpted spark shapes on the body (never transparent bolts, particles, smoke or glow halos); fur, hair and feathers as a few large carved clumps.
